compiled_state.title: [merge-to-main-pr / push workflow]: stale local branch -> push rejected, manual pull --rebase required before PR create/update
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** e7855920a7b5ce38d2043d435568ee439dd8aa56
* **merge.strategy:** pr
* **Affected workflow:** /dso:fix-bug Phase H Step 1 -> COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit: Merging to Main" -> push / PR create
* **Plugin version:** dso-dev v1.16.11

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When a session has just committed a fix locally and intends to push the branch (either to update an existing PR or create a new one), the workflow should:

1. Fetch the remote ref for the target branch
2. If the local branch is behind the remote (i.e., other commits have landed since the session started — common in worktrees that pre-existed earlier merges from main), rebase or merge the remote work into the local branch
3. Resolve any conflicts (autonomously when trivial; via /dso:resolve-conflicts when not)
4. Only THEN run `git push` or `gh pr create`

The pre-push step is the appropriate guard — by the time the orchestrator reaches `git push`, the local branch should already be a fast-forward of the remote.

#### Actual Behavior

The session reached `git push` twice with a stale local branch. Both times the push was rejected (`! [rejected] worktree-... -> worktree-... (fetch first)`) and the orchestrator had to fall back to `git pull --rebase origin <branch>` and re-attempt the push manually. No DSO-shipped step in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md, merge-to-main-pr.sh, or the worktree-isolation harvest path detected the staleness ahead of time.

Specifically observed in this session (worktree `worktree-20260506-111039`):

1. After the first commit (`fix(skill-registration): add debug-everything command...` 4f939b9343), `git push` failed:
   ```
   ! [rejected]              worktree-20260506-111039 -> worktree-20260506-111039 (fetch first)
   error: failed to push some refs
   ```
   Origin had a merge commit `8916244d14 Merge branch 'main' into worktree-20260506-111039` that landed while this session was running. Manual `git pull --rebase origin worktree-20260506-111039` resolved it; second push succeeded.

2. After the second commit (`fix(ci): consolidate ci.yml...` e7855920a7), `git push` failed identically. Origin had `6820cc32bf Merge branch 'main' into worktree-20260506-111039` from a pre-merge sync. Same manual `git pull --rebase` recovery.

This is recurring friction; both the push step and any `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` step that follows should sync the local branch first.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken:**
  * COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md Step 6 created the commit
  * COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit" -> `git push`
  * Push rejected: `! [rejected] ... (fetch first)`
* **Raw Results:**
  * `fatal: bad object 8916244d149507baee58b070477d824fe1367383`
  * `Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally.`
* **Known Workarounds:**
  * `git fetch origin <branch>` then `git pull --rebase origin <branch>` then `git push`. This works for trivial cases (no conflicts) but does NOT scale to conflict-bearing rebases — those would need /dso:resolve-conflicts dispatch, which the workflow doesn't trigger automatically.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit: Merging to Main" section
* plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (`_phase_push` and `_phase_pr_create`)
* /dso:resolve-conflicts (the right escalation target when sync produces conflicts)

### 6. Logs

```
$ git push
fatal: bad object 8916244d149507baee58b070477d824fe1367383
Pre-push format + lint check.............................................Passed
To https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra.git
 ! [rejected]              worktree-20260506-111039 -> worktree-20260506-111039 (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra.git'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not
hint: have locally. This is usually caused by another repository pushing to
hint: the same ref. If you want to integrate the remote changes, use
hint: 'git pull' before pushing again.

$ git pull --rebase origin worktree-20260506-111039
From https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra
 * branch                  worktree-20260506-111039 -> FETCH_HEAD
Rebasing (1/1)Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/worktree-20260506-111039.

$ git push
   8916244d14..4f939b9343  worktree-20260506-111039 -> worktree-20260506-111039
```

#### Suggested fix scope

Add a pre-push sync phase to COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit" and to merge-to-main-pr.sh's `_phase_push` / `_phase_pr_create`:

1. `git fetch origin <head_ref>` (and `origin/main` since merge.strategy=pr targets main)
2. Compare `HEAD` to `origin/<head_ref>` — if behind, attempt `git rebase origin/<head_ref>`
3. If rebase fails with conflicts, dispatch /dso:resolve-conflicts (the workflow already exists for this purpose) instead of crashing or pushing stale work
4. Only after sync succeeds, push and run `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit`

This same logic should apply when creating a NEW PR (gh pr create) — the local HEAD should be a fast-forward of `origin/<head_ref>` and reasonably current with `origin/main` so the PR doesn't open with stale-branch warnings or surprise conflicts.
